# Component library

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-components.mjs from each file's @motomation-component header. Do not edit by hand. -->

68 components across 8 families, written for this skill. Each is one file, typed in strict TypeScript, React only, with no other dependencies. They share small helper files: `_lib/motion.ts` for reduced motion, pointer type, viewport and scroll progress, and `_lib/ambient.ts` (heavy backgrounds only) for the capability probe, DPR clamp and pausing. Every component has props with sensible defaults, a reduced-motion path, a touch behaviour, and notes on when it earns its place and when it's slop.

**References, not a limit.** The components in examples/components/ are references and starting points. They are not a menu. They are not a limit. If the brief needs something that does not exist in the library, build it. Write it as one file, with a header that records tier, use-when, avoid-when, reduced-motion, and touch behaviour, following the same pattern as the library. The skill grows when the agent builds something new.

**Compose, extend, or invent.** Compose a component here when the Thinking Sequence asks for its effect, tune its props to the brief, and keep it inside the tier budget. Extend it (props, timing, a fork with its own header) when it is close. Invent a new one when nothing here fits. The signature move is designed for the brief: if a component here resembles it, bend the component to the concept rather than the other way round. A new component follows the header below (`id`, `name`, `family`, `tier`, `deps`, `what`, `use-when`, `avoid-when`, `reduced-motion`, `touch`, `a11y`); placed in this folder, `node scripts/build-components.mjs` checks the header and regenerates this catalogue, `data/components.csv` and the registry from it.

**Install one into a project:**

```bash
# copy the file plus the _lib helpers it imports into your components folder, or use the registry:
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/main/registry/<id>.json
```

**See them live:** open `examples/gallery/index.html` in a browser (self-contained, no build). Toggle reduced motion in your OS to see every fallback.

## Type

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BlurFocus`](type/blur-focus.tsx) | 2 | Words sharpen from a soft blur into focus, one after another, as the line enters the screen. | The concept is about clarity, focus, eyesight, photography or waking up. | Every heading on the page; long paragraphs; low-end devices with many instances. | Text is sharp and visible from the start. |
| [`CurvedText`](type/curved-text.tsx) | 1 | Text set around a circle like a stamp or seal, with an optional slow turn. | Badges, stamps, seals, "since" marks and a single rotating label beside a primary action. | Anything the reader must read quickly; as a loading spinner; more than one per screen. | The ring is still. |
| [`Decode`](type/decode.tsx) · signature `decode` | 2 | A short label resolves from random glyphs, left to right, when it enters the screen or on hover. | Technical, secret or data-led brands; labels of 1–4 words. | Body text, headlines longer than a line, or more than one per screen. | Shows the final text at once; no glyph cycling. |
| [`InkFill`](type/ink-fill.tsx) · signature `ink-fill` | 2 | A statement starts in the muted colour and fills with ink word by word as the reader scrolls through it. | Manifestos, about statements, a single paragraph that is the page's idea. | More than one per page; text the reader needs before scrolling (it must stay readable when muted). | The whole statement is in ink from the start. |
| [`LetterRelay`](type/letter-relay.tsx) · signature `letter-relay` | 2 | A large hero name shrinks and travels into a fixed header slot letter by letter as you scroll the first screen, so the name hands itself to the navigation. | Portfolios and personal brands where the name is the identity. | Long names (over ~16 characters); pages without a fixed header; product pages. | The hero name and the header name are both static; no scroll listener runs. |
| [`NeighbourMoves`](type/neighbour-moves.tsx) · signature `neighbour-moves` | 2 | Each letter of a name has its own small move on hover (lift, tilt, stretch, spin, drop), so the word feels like a cast of characters. | Personal names, studio names and light-hearted logotypes of 3–12 letters. | Navigation, body text, or brands that must feel calm. | No hover moves. |
| [`PressureType`](type/pressure-type.tsx) | 2 | Each letter of one display word stretches wider and heavier as the cursor nears it, like pressing into rubber. | Playful, elastic or physical brands with a variable font that has wdth and wght axes. | Fonts without variable axes; more than one word; any body copy. | Letters stay at the base width and weight. |
| [`ScrollFloat`](type/scroll-float.tsx) | 2 | Letters of a display line rise and settle into place one by one, driven by scroll position, so scrolling back reverses it. | Light-hearted display lines that should feel buoyant; one line per section. | Serious or institutional briefs; text that must be readable before it settles (prices, dates). | Letters sit in place; no scroll listener runs. |
| [`SplitFlap`](type/split-flap.tsx) | 2 | Each character flips through the alphabet to its value like a departure board, settling left to right; changing the value flips again. | Schedules, line-ups, menus, travel, times and short codes. | Long text; values the reader must trust mid-animation (the final value is announced, not the flips). | Shows the new value at once. |
| [`WidthSprint`](type/width-sprint.tsx) · signature `width-sprint` | 2 | A display word stretches wider the faster you scroll and relaxes back when you stop, using the font's width axis. | Sport, speed, events and launches with a variable font that has a wdth axis. | Fonts without wdth; more than one element; layouts where the word could overflow at its widest. | The word stays at its base width. |

## Text effects

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`AsciiText`](text/ascii-text.tsx) | 2 | A word drawn as a grid of characters, sampled from the word's own letterforms; it settles out of character noise when it enters the screen. | The concept is code, print terminals, telegrams, early computing or textile grids; one short word at display size. | Anything longer than about 12 characters; small sizes (it becomes noise); as the only copy of important text. | The finished character drawing, with no noise. |
| [`Glitch`](text/glitch.tsx) | 2 | On hover, focus or tap, the word tears for a moment: two offset colour copies slip sideways in thin bands, then it settles. Never loops. | The concept is a broken signal, a corrupted file, a jump cut or an error that matters; one word or a short label. | Body text; anything that must be read during the effect; brands that want calm; more than one per page. | Plain text; nothing tears. |
| [`RotatingWords`](text/rotating-words.tsx) | 1 | One word in a sentence turns over to the next, like a rolling counter, a few times, then rests. The slot is as wide as the longest word (with the sentence's ending attached), so nothing around it moves. | The sentence really has several true endings (who you serve, what you make), and the rest of the line stays still. | More than one per page; endings that are adjectives about yourself ("innovative", "bold"); the hero's only message. | The first word, still; all the words are listed for assistive tech. |
| [`ScrambleOnHover`](text/scramble-on-hover.tsx) | 2 | Letters near the pointer scramble into other glyphs, like a magnet passing over iron filings, and settle back as it moves on. Unlike Decode, it reacts locally, where the cursor is. | A short label the visitor plays with (a name, a nav word, a project title) on a code, cipher or signal concept. | Words the visitor must read while pointing at them (buttons with actions); long text; for a one-time reveal (use Decode). | Plain text; nothing scrambles. |
| [`ShinyText`](text/shiny-text.tsx) | 1 | A single band of light passes once across a short label, like light catching foil or a brass plate, when it enters the screen and again on hover. | The material is metal, foil, glass or a printed seal; one short label or badge. | Large headlines (the moving gradient is paint-heavy: cost grows with area); body text; infinite loops; as a "premium" sticker on everything. | Solid ink, no light band. |
| [`Typewriter`](text/typewriter.tsx) | 1 | A line types itself out, character by character, when it scrolls into view, with a caret that fades once the line is complete. | The concept is a terminal, a typed letter, a dispatch or a confession; one line, read once. | Headlines the visitor needs at once; more than one per screen; long paragraphs; anything repeated on every visit. | The whole line is there from the start, with no caret. |

| [`HorizontalReel`](scroll/horizontal-reel.tsx) · signature `horizontal-reel` | 2 | A section pins and vertical scroll pulls a strip of frames sideways, like film through a gate; a frame counter follows. | Film, gallery, timeline and process concepts with 4–10 frames. | Content people need to scan quickly; more than one per page; frames that need reading time. | The frames become a normal horizontally scrollable row with snap points. |
| [`ReadingRail`](scroll/reading-rail.tsx) | 1 | A thin rail at the top or edge of the screen fills as you read an article, with an optional chapter label that changes at each heading. | Long reads, case studies and documentation pages. | Short pages; landing pages; next to another progress indicator. | The rail still reflects progress (it's information, not decoration) but moves in 5% steps instead of continuously. |
| [`StackedDeck`](scroll/stacked-deck.tsx) · signature `stacked-deck` | 2 | Cards stick one after another and stack like a deck; covered cards step back and dim, leaving their titles as a table of contents. | Sequences, case studies, steps and services with 3–6 items. | More than 6 cards; cards taller than the viewport; content that must be compared side by side. | A plain ordered list in normal flow: no sticky, no scale, no dim; every card is a full, readable block. |
| [`Thread`](scroll/thread.tsx) · signature `thread` | 2 | One line draws itself down the page as you scroll, linking sections like a seam, a route or a timeline. | Journeys, timelines, craft (stitching, drawing), routes and process pages. | As decoration on a page without a journey; together with another scroll signature. | The line is fully drawn and still. |
| [`VelocityMarquee`](scroll/velocity-marquee.tsx) | 2 | A looping marquee that drifts on its own, speeds up with scroll speed, follows scroll direction and leans (skews) while you scroll fast. | Sport, launches, events and a single line of brand words between sections. | Content the reader needs (prices, dates); more than one marquee per page. | A static, wrapped row of the same words. |

## Cursor

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ImageTrail`](cursor/image-trail.tsx) | 2 | Moving the cursor across an area drops a trail of images that appear, linger briefly and shrink away, cycling through a set. | Photographers, archives, studios with a deep body of work; one area per page. | Fewer than 5 images; e-commerce product pages; over text that must be read. | The images are shown as a static row instead. |
| [`Lens`](cursor/lens.tsx) · signature `lens` | 2 | A circle follows the cursor and reveals a second layer underneath: sketch under final, night under day, before under after. | The two layers are the story (process, transformation, hidden detail). | The second layer is decoration; text-heavy layers; more than one per page. | The lens jumps to the cursor without easing; a "Show the other layer" toggle shows the second layer at full size. |
| [`PixelWake`](cursor/pixel-wake.tsx) · signature `pixel-wake` | 2 | The cursor leaves a trail of square pixels on a grid that fade out behind it, like a wake on a low-resolution screen. | Digital, pixel, retro, game and screen-themed concepts; usually only over the hero. | Over body text; on calm or luxury briefs; together with another cursor effect. | No trail. |
| [`SeismographLine`](cursor/seismograph-line.tsx) · signature `seismograph-line` | 2 | A hairline divider bends toward the cursor as it passes and springs back with a small wobble, like a needle on a seismograph. | Dividers on calm editorial pages where one living detail is enough; sound, measurement and science brands. | Every divider; busy pages; pages that already have a cursor effect. | A straight line. |
| [`TargetCursor`](cursor/target-cursor.tsx) | 2 | A small crosshair follows the cursor; over anything clickable it snaps out into corner brackets that frame the target. | Precision tools, cameras, games, architecture and engineering concepts. | Content sites; together with another cursor effect; when it would hide the system cursor (it doesn't by default). | Brackets jump to targets without easing. |
| [`TiltCard`](cursor/tilt-card.tsx) | 2 | A card rotates in 3D toward the cursor with a soft moving highlight, like holding a physical card to the light. | Physical objects: tickets, cards, passes, packaging, a single product. | Grids of many cards; text-heavy cards; cards that are links to long content (the motion distracts). | Flat card, no rotation or highlight. |

## Backgrounds

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`Aurora`](backgrounds/aurora.tsx) | 4 | Curtains of northern light hang across a night sky: a sharp lower hem, fading upward in vertical rays, folding slowly. A small WebGL shader draws it; a CSS poster stands in everywhere else. | The subject is the far north, night, cold, observation, polar travel or a planetarium: behind a hero or a single quiet section. | As a generic "AI glow" background; behind body copy; light themes; pages that already run WebGL. | A designed still, not a frozen frame: a long-exposure plate. The curtains settle into three smooth ribbons of the same two colours over a dark ridge, under circular star trails; no canvas is mounted. |
| [`Beams`](backgrounds/beams.tsx) | 4 | Parallel shafts of sunlight fall through a row of high windows (a clerestory, a mill, a stage rig) at one shared angle and sway slightly in depth. CSS 3D only: soft gradient shafts rotated in a perspective space; no WebGL, because transforms are enough here. | Churches, mills, warehouses, galleries, theatres, anything lit through high windows: behind one dark hero. | Bright themes; as "spotlight on our product" decoration; together with other moving backgrounds. | A designed still: noon held. Hard-edged shafts fall through the windows and land as bright pools on the floor, dust caught in the light; not the sway stopped. |
| [`ContourLines`](backgrounds/contour-lines.tsx) | 2 | Topographic contour lines drawn as SVG that slowly drift, like a map breathing; deterministic from a seed. | Landscape, outdoors, climate, geography, agriculture and mapping concepts. | Urban or tech brands without a land story; behind dense text. | Still lines. |
| [`DotField`](backgrounds/dot-field.tsx) | 2 | A grid of dots that swell and push away from the cursor, then ease back, like a pin-art board. | Technical, structural, data or grid-led concepts; behind a hero with little text. | Behind body text; organic or luxury briefs; together with a cursor signature. | A still dot grid. |
| [`Globe`](backgrounds/globe.tsx) | 4 | A sphere of evenly spaced dots turns slowly, the far side faint, with a few brighter markers for real places (lat/lon). WebGL points; a CSS dotted disc stands in everywhere else. | The business is genuinely about places on Earth (shipping, a diaspora, offices in named cities, a travel route), and the markers are real. | As a generic "global" or "scale" signal; with invented markers; on pages that already run WebGL; at small sizes (the dots turn to noise). | A designed still: a chart plate of the globe facing the first marker, drawn in line (graticule, rim, the markers ringed and joined by arcs in order), not the dot sphere stopped. No canvas is mounted. |
| [`Grain`](backgrounds/grain.tsx) | 1 | A film-grain layer over a section or the whole page, static by default or gently flickering at a low frame rate. | Analogue, photographic, warm or printed brands; to take the digital edge off flat colour. | Over small text at high opacity; on clinical, technical brands; animated on low-end mobile. | Static grain. |
| [`Halftone`](backgrounds/halftone.tsx) | 2 | Renders an image as print dots on a canvas, sized by brightness, like a newspaper photo; dots can grow in as it enters the screen. | Print, newspaper, zine, poster, protest and retro concepts. | Product photos people must inspect; portraits where likeness matters; many on one page. | Dots render at full size immediately. |
| [`LightSweep`](backgrounds/light-sweep.tsx) | 1 | A slow band of light crosses a surface every few seconds, like sun moving through a window or a scanner pass. | Architecture, light, time-of-day and hospitality concepts; behind one hero or one card. | Behind text where the band would drop contrast; as a "shimmer" on buttons; more than one per screen. | No sweep. |
| [`LiquidField`](backgrounds/liquid-field.tsx) | 4 | Slow flowing colour like ink in water or silk in wind, drawn by a tiny WebGL fragment shader with a CSS gradient fallback. | The material really is liquid, fabric, light or weather; behind a hero with one line of type. | As generic "AI gradient" decoration; behind body text; on pages that already use WebGL. | A designed still: a marbled sheet. Combed bands of the same three colours, like marbled paper keeping the trace of moving ink; no canvas is mounted. |
| [`MeshGradient`](backgrounds/mesh-gradient.tsx) | 4 | Four soft pools of colour drift very slowly over a ground colour and blend where they meet, like a dyed silk or a weather map. CSS only: each pool is a radial gradient moved with transform; no blur filter, no WebGL. | The palette itself is the brand (a paint, a cosmetics line, a dye house, a weather service), and a calmer, cheaper option than Liquid Field is right. | As the default "modern" hero background; behind body copy; with more than one other effect on the page; with clashing colours (the overlaps make new ones). | A designed still: a colour study. The four colours laid out as soft horizontal fields (horizon, body, ground) with a fine grain; not the drift stopped. |
| [`Meteors`](backgrounds/meteors.tsx) | 4 | Now and then a thin streak of light crosses a night sky at one shared angle and burns out; long quiet gaps between them. CSS only: each streak is a gradient line moved with transform. | Night skies, observatories, wishes, launches that are literal (a rocket club), New Year: behind one dark hero. | As "speed" or "innovation" decoration; light themes; more than one sky per page; busy sections where a flicker at the edge distracts from reading. | A designed still: a long-exposure night, star trails wheeling round the pole and one bright meteor crossing them at the same angle, over a low horizon. The streak tracks are not rendered. |
| [`ParticleField`](backgrounds/particle-field.tsx) | 4 | Dust drifting through a beam of light: soft particles at three depths, the near ones larger and brighter, all moving slowly sideways and bobbing. WebGL points; a CSS poster of scattered motes stands in elsewhere. | Cinema, projection, workshops, old rooms, archives, snowfall or pollen: a quiet atmosphere behind a dark hero. | "Tech" or "data" decoration; as a starfield warp; behind text-heavy sections; on pages that already run WebGL. For a cursor-reactive grid use Dot Field. | A designed still: a star chart. The motes keep their density and depth, and a few are joined into constellations; no canvas is mounted. |

## Layout and galleries

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BentoReveal`](layout/bento-reveal.tsx) | 1 | A modular grid of mixed-size tiles that enter in reading order with a short stagger the first time the grid scrolls in. | Content that truly has mixed weights (one big feature, several small facts). | Equal-weight content (use a list); as the default landing layout (it's overused); more than one per page. | Tiles are visible from the start. |
| [`CurveCarousel`](layout/curve-carousel.tsx) | 2 | Cards sit on a shallow arc; the focused card is upright and in front, its neighbours tilt and recede. Arrow keys, buttons, drag and swipe move it. | 3–9 case studies or products where one at a time is the point. | Content people need to compare; more than 9 items; as autoplaying decoration. | Cards change position without easing. |
| [`Dock`](layout/dock.tsx) | 2 | A row of icon buttons that magnify smoothly as the cursor passes along them, neighbours growing a little less. | App-like tool collections, launchers and playful personal sites with 4–8 actions. | Primary navigation that needs labels; touch-first sites; more than 8 items. | No magnification. |
| [`FlowingMenu`](layout/flowing-menu.tsx) | 2 | A big typographic list of links; hovering an item rolls a band over it from the edge the cursor entered, carrying a marquee of the item's words. | Portfolio and studio navigation or project indexes with 3–8 entries. | Primary site navigation on product sites; long lists; touch-first audiences. | Hover shows the band instantly with still text. |
| [`InfiniteCanvas`](layout/infinite-canvas.tsx) | 2 | Drag (or use arrow keys) to pan an endless wall of tiles that repeats in every direction, with a little momentum when you let go. | The Gallery Wall archetype: archives, pin boards, studios with lots of visual work. | Fewer than ~12 tiles; content that needs order; as the only way to reach the work (also provide a list). | No momentum; panning still works. |
| [`StickyIndex`](layout/sticky-index.tsx) | 1 | A sticky side index lists the page's sections and highlights the one you are reading, with a marker that slides between entries. | Long case studies, reports, documentation, annual reviews. | Short pages; mobile (it collapses to a top select); landing pages. | The marker jumps instead of sliding. |

## Buttons, cards and UI

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`AnimatedList`](ui/animated-list.tsx) | 1 | Entries arrive one at a time, like orders coming into a kitchen or messages into a log: each slides up into its slot and settles. It plays once, then the list is simply a list. | The content really arrives over time (orders, sign-ups, sensor readings, a changelog), and showing the arrival explains the product. | Fake "live activity" or social proof; long lists (over about 8 entries); content the visitor needs to scan at once. | Every entry is there from the start. |
| [`useConfetti`](ui/confetti.tsx) | 2 | Paper pieces burst from a point, tumble and flutter down under gravity and air drag, and are gone in under two seconds. Fired by you, from code, at a real moment. | A genuine, rare success the visitor caused: an order placed, a donation made, a course finished, a wedding RSVP. Once. | Page load; every button; form validation; serious contexts (payments for bills, health, legal); repeated triggers. For small click feedback use Click Spark. | No particles at all; your success message carries the moment. |
| [`DeviceMockup`](ui/device-mockup.tsx) | 1 | A phone, browser or laptop frame drawn in CSS around real content (a screenshot or live markup). For a tall screenshot, pointing at the screen scrolls it slowly to the bottom, like someone reading. | Showing the actual product screen (an app, a site you built) where the device tells the visitor where it runs. | Stock "phone with a gradient" decoration; floating several devices at angles; screens with fake data; when the screen alone, unframed, reads better. | A tall screen shows its whole page, still; any other screen can be scrolled with the wheel or keyboard. |
| [`GlareCard`](ui/glare-card.tsx) | 2 | A flat, laminated card with a foil sheen: a soft band of colour and a sharp white glint slide across it as the pointer moves, the way a hologram on an ID card or a trading card catches light. The card itself never tilts (for tilt, use Tilt Card). | Passes, tickets, membership cards, collectibles, certificates: one small card that is a physical object. | Large surfaces (the blend is paint-heavy: its cost grows with area); photos of people; grids of many cards; anything that must look sober. | A still, faint sheen at one angle; no glint movement. |
| [`GlowBorder`](ui/glow-border.tsx) | 1 | The edge of a card lights up nearest the pointer, as if the pointer were a lamp held close to it; the light fades along the edge with distance. Only the border glows, never the surface. | A row or grid of dark cards or inputs where the pointer's position should feel physical (a control panel, a studio's service list, pricing tiers). | Light themes with low-contrast borders; single cards (no neighbours to compare); a page already using Spotlight Card on the same cards. | A steady, faint border. |
| [`IconCloud`](ui/icon-cloud.tsx) | 2 | Labels or small icons sit on the surface of an invisible ball that turns slowly; dragging spins it and it coasts to a stop. The near side is large and sharp, the far side small and faint. | A collection the visitor browses for the pleasure of it (a herbarium's species, a type foundry's glyphs, a band's setlist history), with the full list available in text. | A logo wall of "technologies we use"; as navigation; more than about 40 items; small screens where a plain list reads better (below 300px wide it falls back to a wrapped list). | The ball, still, at a fixed angle; dragging still turns it (the visitor's own motion). |
| [`LoaderSkeleton`](ui/loader-skeleton.tsx) | 1 | Grey placeholder shapes in the exact layout of the content that's coming (an avatar, a title, a few lines), with a faint light passing over them, so the page doesn't jump when the content lands. | Content whose layout you know is loading (a card, a list row, a profile, an article), for waits over about 300ms. | Waits you can't predict the shape of (use Loader Spinner); placeholders that don't match the real layout (they cause the jump they're meant to prevent); whole pages of skeletons. | The same shapes, with no passing light. |
| [`LoaderSpinner`](ui/loader-spinner.tsx) | 1 | A thin ring whose arc stretches and shortens as it turns, for waits of unknown length. It only appears after a short delay, so fast loads never flash a spinner. | A wait you can't measure (a search, a payment check) inside a button, a panel or a page area. | Waits you can measure (show progress instead); content loading where the layout is known (use Loader Skeleton); whole-page splash screens. | The ring holds still at three-quarters and the label is shown; nothing turns. |
| [`OrbitingCircles`](ui/orbiting-circles.tsx) | 2 | Small badges travel on one or two thin circular orbits around a centre, staying upright as they go; the outer ring turns the other way, more slowly. Pointing at it stops the orbits. | A real centre with real satellites: a cooperative and its member farms, a studio and its long-term clients, a hub airport and its routes. | The generic "integrations around our logo" picture; more than about 10 satellites; anything the visitor must read while it moves (list them in text too). | The same arrangement, still. |
| [`RainbowBorder`](ui/rainbow-border.tsx) | 1 | A thin border made of a turning colour wheel around a card or button. It turns while you point at or focus the element and rests otherwise. | One element that is literally about colour (a paint, a print shop, a palette tool, a pride event), or the single "new" item in a list. | As generic "AI glow"; on more than one element per screen; serious or quiet brands; around body text blocks. | The same colour border, still. |
| [`ShimmerButton`](ui/shimmer-button.tsx) | 1 | A button that a narrow band of light crosses once when you point at it or focus it, and that presses down slightly when clicked. | The one primary action on a dark or metallic surface (book, reserve, buy) where a little glint suits the material. | More than one per screen; secondary actions; a page already using Light Sweep; light, paper-like brands (the glint reads as plastic). | No band; the press still darkens the button (colour, not movement). |
| [`SpotlightCard`](ui/spotlight-card.tsx) | 1 | A dark card with a soft pool of light that follows the pointer across its surface, like a torch on a wall. | Night, theatre, cinema, exhibition or archive concepts: a grid of a few dark cards the visitor explores. | Light surfaces (the pool vanishes); a grid where every card already moves; content that must be read evenly lit. | A fixed, soft pool near the top of the card. |
| [`Terminal`](ui/terminal.tsx) | 1 | A terminal window replays a short session when it scrolls into view: each command types itself after the prompt, its output appears at once, then the next command starts. | The product really is used from a command line (a CLI, a dev tool, an install step), and the session shown is real and copy-pasteable. | As "techy" decoration for a product with no CLI; sessions longer than about 8 lines; fake output. | The whole session is shown at once. |

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BrandSelection`](micro/brand-selection.tsx) · signature `brand-selection` | 1 | Text selection uses the brand accent and ink instead of the browser's blue, scoped to a section or the whole page. | Almost always; it's a tiny, free detail that shows care. | The accent and its text colour don't pass 4.5:1 together. | Not applicable (no motion). |

## Anatomy of a component

Every file starts with the same header, which this catalogue, `data/components.csv` and the registry are generated from. `check-repo` fails if a field is missing or the catalogue is stale.

```tsx
"use client";
// @motomation-component
// id: …
// name: …
// family: …
// tier: …
// deps: …
// what: …
// use-when: …
// avoid-when: …
// reduced-motion: …
// touch: …
// a11y: …
```

Rules for new components: one exported function component, props with defaults, no dependency beyond React unless the tier needs it, a reduced-motion path in code, cleanup of every listener and frame loop, decorative layers `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`, and original code only.

## Right-to-left

Every text, type and layout component works on a right-to-left page (`<html dir="rtl">` or any ancestor with `dir`/`direction`), with nothing to configure; `tests/components/rtl.test.mjs` checks each one against an LTR control. The rules, for new components too:

- Layout uses logical properties (`inset-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `border-inline-start`), never `left`/`right` for something that belongs to the reading start or end.
- Text split into letters or words (inline-blocks or flex items) sits inside a `dir="auto"` wrapper: split boxes are bidi-neutral, so without it a Latin word on an Arabic page shows reversed and a Hebrew phrase on an English page shows its words in the wrong order. A string that mixes directions inside one split run is ordered by its first strong letter; keep mixed strings in plain text.
- What layout cannot mirror is read from `useDirection(ref)` or `isRtl(el)` (`_lib/motion.ts`): pointer x to letter index, the meaning of ← → and of a swipe, the direction a sweep, marquee or relay travels.
- Pictures stay pictures: an ASCII drawing, a canvas or a map is laid out left to right (`dir="ltr"`) whatever the page.
